labels.text: Transfer-Encoding was added in HTTP/1.1. It is generally assumed that implementations
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: advertising only HTTP/1.0 support will not understand how to process transfer-encoded content,
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: and that an HTTP/1.0 message received with a Transfer-Encoding is likely to have been forwarded
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: without proper handling ofthe chunked transfer coding in transit.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: A client MUST NOT send a request containing Transfer-Encoding unless it knows the server will
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: handle HTTP/1.1 requests (or later minor revisions); such knowledge might be in the form of
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: speciﬁc user conﬁguration or by remembering the version of a prior received response. A server
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: MUST NOT send a response containing Transfer-Encoding unless the corresponding request
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: indicates HTTP/1.1 (or later minor revisions).
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Early implementations ofTransfer-Encoding would occasionally send both a chunked transfer
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: coding for message framing and an estimated Content-Length header ﬁeld for use by progress
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: bars. This is why Transfer-Encoding is deﬁned as overriding Content-Length, as opposed to them
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: being mutually incompatible. Unfortunately, forwarding such a message can lead to
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: vulnerabilities regarding request smuggling (Section 11.2) or response splitting (Section 11.1)
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: attacks if any downstream recipient fails to parse the message according to this speciﬁcation,
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: particularly when a downstream recipient only implements HTTP/1.0.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: A server MAY reject a request that contains both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding or
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: process such a request in accordance with the Transfer-Encoding alone. Regardless, the server
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: MUST close the connection after responding to such a request to avoid the potential attacks.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: A server or client that receives an HTTP/1.0 message containing a Transfer-Encoding header ﬁeld
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: MUST treat the message as ifthe framing is faulty, even if a Content-Length is present, and close
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: the connection after processing the message. The message sender might have retained a portion
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: ofthe message, in buﬀer, that could be misinterpreted by further use ofthe connection.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: 6.2. Content-Length
labels.rationale: Section heading "6.2. Content-Length"

labels.text: When a message does not have a Transfer-Encoding header ﬁeld, a Content-Length header ﬁeld
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: (Section 8.6 of [HTTP]) can provide the anticipated size, as a decimal number of octets, for
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: potential content. For messages that do include content, the Content-Length ﬁeld value provides
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: the framing information necessary for determining where the data (and message) ends. For
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: messages that do not include content, the Content-Length indicates the size ofthe selected
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: representation (Section 8.6 of [HTTP]).
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: A sender MUST NOT send a Content-Length header ﬁeld in any message that contains a Transfer-
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Encoding header ﬁeld.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Note: HTTP's use of Content-Length for message framing diﬀers signiﬁcantly from
labels.rationale: Indented note "Note: HTTP's use of Content-Length ..." (body note)

labels.text: the same ﬁeld's use in MIME, where it is an optional ﬁeld used only within the
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: C.2.1. Multihomed Web Servers
labels.rationale: Subsection heading "C.2.1. Multihomed Web Servers"

labels.text: The requirements that clients and servers support the Host header ﬁeld (Section 7.2 of [HTTP]),
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: report an error ifit is missing from an HTTP/1.1 request, and accept absolute URIs (Section 3.2)
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: are among the most important changes deﬁned by HTTP/1.1.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Older HTTP/1.0 clients assumed a one-to-one relationship ofIP addresses and servers; there was
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: no established mechanism for distinguishing the intended server of a request other than the IP
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: address to which that request was directed. The Host header ﬁeld was introduced during the
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: development ofHTTP/1.1 and, though it was quickly implemented by most HTTP/1.0 browsers,
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: additional requirements were placed on all HTTP/1.1 requests in order to ensure complete
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: adoption. At the time ofthis writing, most HTTP-based services are dependent upon the Host
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: header ﬁeld for targeting requests.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: C.2.2. Keep-Alive Connections
labels.rationale: Subsection heading "C.2.2. Keep-Alive Connections"

labels.text: In HTTP/1.0, each connection is established by the client prior to the request and closed by the
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: server after sending the response. However, some implementations implement the explicitly
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: negotiated ("Keep-Alive") version ofpersistent connections described in Section 19.7.1 of
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page
Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Some clients and servers might wish to be compatible with these previous approaches to
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: persistent connections, by explicitly negotiating for them with a "Connection: keep-alive" request
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: header ﬁeld. However, some experimental implementations ofHTTP/1.0 persistent connections
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: are faulty; for example, if an HTTP/1.0 proxy server doesn't understand Connection, it will
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: erroneously forward that header ﬁeld to the next inbound server, which would result in a hung
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: connection.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: One attempted solution was the introduction of a Proxy-Connection header ﬁeld, targeted
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: speciﬁcally at proxies. In practice, this was also unworkable, because proxies are often deployed
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: in multiple layers, bringing about the same problem discussed above.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: As a result, clients are encouraged not to send the Proxy-Connection header ﬁeld in any requests.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: Clients are also encouraged to consider the use of "Connection: keep-alive" in requests carefully;
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: while they can enable persistent connections with HTTP/1.0 servers, clients using them will need
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: to monitor the connection for "hung" requests (which indicate that the client ought to stop
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: sending the header ﬁeld), and this mechanism ought not be used by clients at all when a proxy is
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: being used.
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: C.2.3. Introduction ofTransfer-Encoding
labels.rationale: Subsection heading "C.2.3. Introduction of Transfer-Encoding"

labels.text: HTTP/1.1 introduces the Transfer-Encoding header ﬁeld (Section 6.1). Transfer codings need to be
labels.rationale: Default: body text, list item, table cell, page number or other non-heading content on this page

labels.text: decoded prior to forwarding an HTTP message over a MIME-compliant protocol.
